extracted.intended_audience: rOpenSci editors (or editorial staff) recruiting peer reviewers for rOpenSci R packages
extracted.subtask_short: recruiting peer reviewers for R packages
extracted.subtask_description: Email-based template and associated expectations for recruiting and onboarding reviewers to perform open peer reviews of rOpenSci R packages via GitHub. Covers what to include in an invitation, timing expectations, conduct rules, and available reviewer support/mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email invitation contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Template elements to include in the invitation: greeting to [REVIEWER], identify yourself as [EDITOR], optional friendly banter, state the package name [PACKAGE], author(s) [AUTHOR(S)], a short description of what the package does [FUNCTION], provide the GitHub repository link [REPO LINK], and link to the onboarding issue for the open review [ONBOARDING ISSUE].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear context and direct links so the reviewer can quickly access the package and the GitHub issue where the review will be conducted. Use the provided placeholders to fill in package-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review completion timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: If you accept, note that we ask reviewers to complete reviews in three weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template notes: "We’ve found it takes a similar amount of time to review a package as an academic paper." Use the three-week target when committing to a review and plan workload accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response-to-invitation timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: If I don't hear from you within a week, I will assume you are unable to review at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors use a one-week window for initial acceptance/decline responses; if no reply is received the invitation is considered declined so editors can recruit alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest check
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure you do not have a conflict of interest preventing you from reviewing this package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult rOpenSci's conflict-of-interest policy (link provided in template) before accepting. If a COI exists, decline or disclose it so the editor can decide on assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewer and packaging guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reviewers guide details what we look for in a package review, and includes links to example reviews. Our standards are detailed in our packaging guide, and we provide a reviewer template for you to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to consult the linked reviewers guide, packaging guide, and reviewer template while performing the review. These resources provide criteria, examples, and a structured template to ensure consistency and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, non-adversarial, improvement-focused tone
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim for reviews to be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality. Be respectful and kind!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should prioritize constructive feedback aimed at improving the package. Follow the reviewers guide and rOpenSci code of conduct (link provided) for expectations about respectful behavior and community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: GitHub-based open review process
rubrics_metrics.description: We conduct our open review process via GitHub as well, here: [ONBOARDING ISSUE].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All review interactions occur on GitHub (issues, PRs). Reviewers should be comfortable using GitHub for comments, suggestions, and review threads; follow the onboarding issue instructions for the specific package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship availability for first-time reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If mentorship requested: the editor offers to be a resource during the process, including answering questions by email and Slack, sharing draft reviews for feedback before posting, and offering a brief videocall to walk through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-time reviewers who requested mentorship may use the editor as a contact, will receive a Slack invite, can share draft reviews for feedback, and may schedule a videocall. Editors should offer these supports when indicated by the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alternate reviewer suggestions when declining
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can not, suggestions for alternate reviewers are always helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When declining an invitation, reviewers are encouraged (but not required) to suggest other qualified reviewers to help editors find replacements quickly.
